title: Describing What's Happening Around Me
writingModel: Snapshot: WKU Library, Thursday at 6 p.m.

I am sitting at my usual desk by the window in the WKU library. It is Thursday evening and the library is fairly busy. I am working on a grammar assignment, but right now I am taking a short break to look around me and describe what is happening.

Directly to my left, a young woman is studying very intensely — she has three textbooks open at the same time and she is writing quickly in a notebook. She is not paying attention to anything around her. Across the table, two students are having a quiet conversation. They are comparing notes from today's lecture and occasionally pointing at something on one of their laptops.

Near the entrance, a librarian is helping a group of first-year students find their seats. She is speaking patiently and pointing to different sections of the library. One of the first-year students is looking quite nervous — he is gripping his bag tightly and looking around with wide eyes. It is probably his first time in the university library.

Outside the window, I can see the university garden. A few students are sitting on benches, even though it is quite cold. One of them is reading a book and the others are talking. In the distance, I can see the lights of the main building beginning to switch on as the sky is getting darker.

Right now, the whole library feels calm and productive. Everyone around me is focused on something. The only sounds are the quiet turning of pages, the soft clicking of keyboards, and the occasional whisper. I find it a good environment to work in. In fact, I am going to close this description now and get back to my grammar assignment — which is waiting patiently for me.
